channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: FDA finally embraces harm reduction, sees role for vaping | Opinion
item.description: Tobacco control embracing harm reduction would mark a shift from fighting nicotine use in the abstract to reducing the harms that actually kill. FDA vaping policy should recognise that adult smokers need legal, evidence-based alternatives capable of moving them away from combustion. That does not weaken prevention or youth protection; it makes the overall strategy more realistic. Public health progress depends on helping people stop smoking, not on treating every nicotine product as the same threat. (Published on September 21, 2026bydesmoinesregister.com)

item.title: Mike Bloomberg's gift to Big Tobacco
item.description: Tobacco control can end up protecting cigarettes even when that is the opposite of its intention. Policies that restrict or stigmatise lower-risk nicotine alternatives may leave combustible tobacco with less competition and adult smokers with fewer viable exits. That is the uncomfortable contradiction at the heart of many anti-vaping campaigns. Public health should scrutinise industry influence, but it should also ask whether its own strategies are keeping the most harmful product in the strongest position. (Published on September 21, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: Science Inside | NicoLeaks Supercharges Nicotine Pouch Testing | RegWatch
item.description: Nicotine pouch testing should be driven by science, not suspicion by category. Better data on ingredients, emissions, exposure and product performance can help regulators distinguish between responsible smoke-free products and those that fail basic standards. That matters because credible harm reduction depends on transparency as much as access. The stronger the testing framework, the harder it becomes to dismiss pouches with fear — or to defend products that do not meet the evidence. (Published on September 21, 2026byregulatorwatch.com)

item.title: Alex Wodak: ‘The safer nicotine option should be the easier option’
item.description: The safer nicotine option should be the easier option. That principle is simple, but many policies still do the opposite by keeping cigarettes familiar, affordable or accessible while making lower-risk alternatives harder to find or understand. Adult smokers need a path away from combustion that is practical in the real world, not only acceptable in theory. Harm reduction works best when regulation makes the less harmful choice the obvious one. (Published on September 21, 2026bysnusforumet.se)
